title: Genetic Information, Variation and Biodiversity
seo_title: Year 12 A Level Biology: Genetic Information and Variation Worksheets
standard_code: A level Biology: Genetic information, variation and relationships between organisms
standard_text: DNA, genes and chromosomes, protein synthesis (transcription and translation), mutations and meiosis, genetic diversity and natural selection, species and classification, and measuring biodiversity.
meta_desc: Free Year 12 A level biology worksheets on genetic information: the genetic code, transcription, translation, meiosis, mutation, classification and Simpson's index. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Gamete combinations = 2ⁿ, where n is the number of chromosome pairs.
body_html:
How to think about it

A gene is a sequence of bases coding for a polypeptide. In transcription, mRNA is made complementary to the template strand (U replaces T). In translation, tRNA anticodons pair with mRNA codons; each triplet codes for one amino acid. Only exons are translated.

Meiosis makes four genetically different haploid cells through crossing over and independent segregation (2ⁿ combinations). Simpson's index D = 1 − Σn(n − 1)/N(N − 1) measures diversity: closer to 1 means more diverse.

Example

Template TAC GGA: mRNA?

complement with U for A

Answer: AUG CCU

Example

2n = 8. Gamete combinations?

n = 4

2⁴

Answer: 16

Common mistakes

  • Writing T instead of U in mRNA.
  • Using 2n instead of n in 2ⁿ.
  • Using N² instead of N(N − 1) in Simpson's index.

faq.q: Why is the genetic code degenerate?
faq.a: Most amino acids are coded for by more than one triplet, so some base substitutions have no effect.

faq.q: What does a high Simpson's index mean?
faq.a: The community is diverse: many species with similar numbers of individuals.

items.q: A gene is 1,800 bases long. How many amino acids does it code for? (Ignore start and stop codons.)
Why is the genetic code described as non-overlapping?
c: only half the bases are read
each base is read in only one triplet
items.e: Triplets are read one after another.

items.q: A gene is 3,000 bases long, of which 300 bases are in introns. How many amino acids does it code for? (Ignore start and stop codons.)
Why is the genetic code described as universal?
c: all organisms have the same genes
the same triplets code for the same amino acids in almost all organisms
items.e: This is evidence of a common origin.

items.q: How is DNA stored in eukaryotic cells?
c: as short circular molecules without proteins
as long linear molecules wound around histone proteins
items.e: Prokaryotes have circular DNA not linked to histones.

items.q: A gene is 3,000 bases long. How many amino acids does it code for? (Ignore start and stop codons.)
What is a homologous pair of chromosomes?
c: two chromosomes with the same genes at the same loci
a pair of sex chromosomes only

items.q: Which mutation is most likely to change many amino acids?
items.e: Every codon after it is changed.

items.q: What does RNA polymerase do?
c: joins RNA nucleotides complementary to the template strand

A gene is 1,200 bases long, of which 90 bases are in introns. How many amino acids does it code for? (Ignore start and stop codons.)
What happens during translation?
c: tRNA anticodons pair with mRNA codons and amino acids are joined by peptide bonds
items.e: ATP is used to attach amino acids to tRNA.

items.q: Where else is DNA found in eukaryotic cells?
items.e: This DNA is short and circular, like prokaryote DNA.

items.q: Why is the genetic code described as degenerate?
c: most amino acids are coded for by more than one triplet
each triplet codes for several amino acids
items.e: There are 64 triplets and 20 amino acids.

items.q: What is a phylogenetic classification based on?
How does crossing over create genetic variation?

items.q: A gamete of a plant has 3 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in a cell after mitosis in this organism?
What is non-disjunction?

items.e: Down's syndrome is caused by an extra chromosome 21.

items.q: Why is random sampling used to measure biodiversity?
c: to choose the most interesting sites

items.q: What is independent segregation?
c: homologous pairs line up and separate randomly in meiosis I
items.e: Each gamete gets a random mix of maternal and paternal chromosomes.

What is a species?
c: a group of populations that cannot breed
a group of organisms that can interbreed to give fertile offspring
items.e: Mules are infertile, so horses and donkeys are different species.

c: natural selection in a large population
a small group starts a new population, so it has little genetic diversity
items.e: Some alleles may become common by chance.
